metadata.change_reason: Architecture invariants quality standard: Comprehensive coverage across nine core dimensions with physical defense mechanisms and clear remediations

spec.name: Nine-Dimension Panoramic Architecture Invariants Quality Standard
spec.objective: Ensure all physical laws of the system—from layering and compatibility to storage, concurrency, code engineering, resilience, and observability—are formally specified with deterministic physical defense and remediation mechanisms
principles: Nine-Dimension Panoramic Coverage: Full coverage across compatibility, layering, storage, concurrency, security, performance, code engineering, resilience, and observability

Architect-Led Engineering Defense: Code quality (Zero Panic/memory safety/static linting) and runtime ops (TraceID propagation/circuit breaking/graceful shutdown) must be enforced by architect-defined invariants

Physical Defense Mechanisms: Every architecture invariant must be implemented via database constraints, compiler flags, linter rules, gateway filters, type systems, concurrency locks, circuit breakers, or telemetry interceptors
Deterministic Remediation: Every invariant must provide deterministic interception, degradation, rollback, or alerting compensation plans
Zero Placeholders: Any TBD, To Be Determined, or unconfirmed placeholders are strictly prohibited

review_dimensions.name: Nine Dimensions Full Coverage
review_dimensions.description: Whether all nine core architectural invariant dimensions are comprehensively covered

review_dimensions.name: Physical Defense Feasibility
review_dimensions.description: Whether defense mechanisms possess explicit technical implementation carriers (DB/Linter/Gateway/Circuit Breaker/Middleware)

review_dimensions.name: Violation Remediation Completeness
review_dimensions.description: Whether remediation strategies possess high operational feasibility and determinism

review_dimensions.name: PRD Requirement & Product Invariant Alignment
review_dimensions.description: Whether aligned with PRD requirements and product invariants
